{{Quote|The Sith reached other worlds, including those outside the Stygian Caldera. Tund became a prison for heretics. Arorua housed monsters that were spawned from Sith sorcery. And the worlds of Malachor and Thule were fortified against counterattack from any foe.|A mention of Tund extracted from the [[Sorzus Syn's chronicle|Chronicle]] of ''[[Jen'jidai]]'' [[Sorzus Syn]], [[6900 BBY]]|<ref name="BoS" />}}
'''Tund''' was a verdant terrestrial [[Planet/Legends|planet]] and potent [[Vergence/Legends|Force nexus]] situated upon the north-eastern borders of the [[Open Sea/Legends|Open Sea]] in the [[Centrality/Legends|Centrality sector]]. A remote colony world of the [[Sith (species)/Legends|Sith species]] first settled around [[27,700 BBY]], Tund saw use as a prison for heretics and exiles prior to the collapse of the [[Sith Empire/Legends|old Sith Empire]], and subsequently came to serve as both the headquarters of the Sith-blooded [[Sorcerers of Tund/Legends|Sorcerers of Tund]] and the adopted homeworld of the [[Toong/Legends|Toong species]]. The planet was [[Destruction of Tund|destroyed]] in [[5 BBY/Legends|5 BBY]] by a [[Rokur Gepta's biological weapon|biological warhead]] released by the [[Croke]] Sorcerer of Tund [[Rokur Gepta]].

Tund was first discovered and colonized around 27,700 BBY by a [[Kissai heretics|group of exiled Sith]] belonging to the [[Kissai]] [[Priest/Legends|priest]] caste. These outcasts were banished from the Sith homeworld of [[Korriban/Legends|Korriban]] for interpreting the death of [[Sith King]] [[Adas]] during the [[Infinite Empire/Legends|Infinite Empire's]] [[Invasion of Korriban|failed invasion]] as a sign from [[The Force/Legends|the Force]] to reject the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]]. Fleeing [[Sith Worlds/Legends|Sith space]] aboard a [[Rakatan ship]] equipped with a [[Force-drive|Force-powered hyperdrive]], these Kissai followed the Force to the hidden world of Tund in the [[Centrality/Legends#Astrography|Centrality sector]], remaining in seclusion for millennia.

Later generations of Sith belonging to both the [[Sith Empire (Pre-Republic)|ancient Sith Empire]] and old Sith Empire used Tund as a penal colony for the imprisonment of their own heretics and exiles. Following the [[6900 BBY]] conquest of Sith space by the [[Human/Legends|Human-blooded]] [[Dark Jedi/Legends|Dark Jedi]] [[Exiles]], Tund's pureblooded Sith were joined on-world by disparate groups of [[Hybrid/Legends|half-breed]] Sith-Human colonists. While many of these half-breeds were outcasts banished from the Sith Worlds, a number of Sith refugees fleeing the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Republic]] [[Post–Great Hyperspace War counterinvasion|counterinvasion]] that followed the [[Great Hyperspace War/Legends|Great Hyperspace War]] likewise settled Tund in the aftermath of the Sith Empire's collapse.

These disparate traditions eventually coalesced to form the Sorcerers of Tund, a sect of Sith-blooded Force users who denied the existence of the [[Light side of the Force/Legends|light]] and dark sides of the Force. Though these Sith remained isolated on their remote world for millennia, they were joined in [[45 BBY/Legends|45 BBY]] by Toong refugees fleeing the devastation of [[Toong'l/Legends|Toong'l]]. The Sorcerers persecuted their new neighbors, but were themselves rendered extinct by the actions of one of their own. [[Rokur Gepta]], a Croke who had infiltrated the group to learn its secrets, killed the Sorcerers and destroyed Tund with a biological weapon in 5 BBY to ensure their knowledge remained exclusively his, bringing an end to the Sith colony that had persisted for over two dozen millennia.

==Description==
{{Quote|Today the planet Tund in the Outer Rim is an uninhabited, irradiated wasteland, but for thousands of years the once lush world was home to a group of Force-users known as the Sorcerers of Tund...|An extract from [[Tionne Solusar]]'s [[40 ABY/Legends|40 ABY]] compendium, ''[[Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force]]''|<ref name="JvS" />}}
Tund was the sole [[Planet/Legends|planet]] of the [[Tund system/Legends|Tund system]], a remote [[Star system/Legends|star system]] situated upon the north-eastern borders of the [[Open Sea/Legends|Open Sea]]<ref name="ACGttC">{{GamerCite|5|A Campaign Guide to the Centrality}}</ref> in the [[Centrality/Legends|Centrality sector]] of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]]. Tund rotated on its axis every forty-eight [[Standard hour/Legends|standard hours]] and orbited its sun, a [[Star/Legends|star]] likewise called [[Tund (star)|Tund]], every one thousand, seven hundred and seventy [[Local day/Legends|local days]] on average. A relatively standard-sized terrestrial world, Tund possessed a planetary diameter of twelve thousand, one hundred and ninety [[Kilometer/Legends|kilometers]].<ref name="TEA" />

For much of its history, Tund was a verdant [[Vergence/Legends|Force nexus]] possessed of a potent connection to the [[Living Force/Legends|Living Force]] generated by its rich ecosphere and diverse assortment of biomes.<ref name="JvS" /> The planet's shadowy [[Jungle/Legends|jungles]] and dark [[Forest/Legends|forests]] teemed with a disparate multiplicity of lifeforms, ranging in form and variety from thick-leafed vines to hard-shelled arthropods.<ref name="TEA" /> Tund's planetary topography was characterized by expansive prairies<ref name="TCSWEIII267" /> and flatlands punctuated at length by plunging cliffs and escarpments, some of which played host to waterfalls<ref name="JATM" /> marking the termini of Tund's rivers.<ref name="TEA" />

However, following [[Rokur Gepta]]'s [[Destruction of Tund|destruction of the planet]] in [[5 BBY/Legends|5 BBY]] by means of an [[electromagnetic torpedo]] and [[Rokur Gepta's biological weapon|biological weapon]], Tund was reduced to a barren, radioactive wasteland devoid of all life. Apart from a small section of the planet protected by Gepta's system of [[Force field/Legends|force fields]],<ref name="TCSWEIII267" /><ref name="NEGtC">''[[The New Essential Guide to Characters]]''</ref> Tund's atmosphere was highly poisonous and contaminated with deadly radiation from the fallout.<ref name="TEA" /><ref name="JvS" />

==History==
===Pre-Republic era===
{{Quote|The Sorcerers of Tund are believed to be the descendants of pureblooded Sith exiled from Korriban long ago...|An extract from [[Chief Librarian/Legends|Chief Librarian]] [[Restelly Quist/Legends|Restelly Quist's]] "The History of the Sith" as published in ''[[The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force]]''|<ref name="TJP" />}}
During the [[pre-Republic era]] prior to the rise of the [[Rakata/Legends|Rakata]] [[Infinite Empire/Legends|Infinite Empire]], the [[Sharu/Legends|Sharu]], a [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoid]] species hailing from [[Rafa V]],<ref name="ACGttC" /> dominated the region of space that in subsequent millennia would be known as the [[Centrality/Legends|Centrality]], circumscribing the remote world of Tund within the bounds of their ancient civilization.<ref name="TEA" /> Though the Sharu were believed to have voluntarily abandoned their holdings and withdrawn to their ancestral homeworld in fear of the [[Celestial/Legends|Celestials]],<ref name="TEGtWAC">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-essential-guide-to-warfare-authors-cut-the-celestials|text=''Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare'' Author's Cut &mdash; The Celestials|int=Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare Author's Cut}}</ref> the legacy of the Sharu endured on Tund, where [[Old High Trammic/Legends|Old High Trammic]]&mdash;a trade language descended from the original tongue of the Sharu<ref name="ACGttC" />&mdash;continued to see regular usage in subsequent millennia.<ref name="TEA" />

Sometime prior to [[27,700 BBY]],<ref name="JvS" /> the Rakata discovered [[Korriban/Legends|Korriban]], the ancestral [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] of the [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]] [[Sith (species)/Legends|Sith species]].<ref name="TCSWEII227">{{CSWECite|II|227|Korriban}}</ref> In an effort to secure the allegiance of the Sith, the Rakata plied and seduced the [[Sith King]] [[Adas]] with gifts of [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark-sided]] knowledge and technology, teaching the Sith King to create [[Holocron of King Adas|his own holocron]] for the storage of his teachings.<ref name="END">{{Hyperspace|url=hyperspace/member/insideronline/88/indexp2.html|text=''Evil Never Dies: The Sith Dynasties''|int=Evil Never Dies: The Sith Dynasties}}</ref> Though the Sith had long engaged in sortilege, civil war, and sentient sacrifice, they led spiritually serene lives, never once doubting or questioning the critical role conflict played in their kratocratic society. It was only with the introduction of the Rakatans' methodic malice that the Sith first fell to the dark side.<ref name="KOTORCGWE5" />

In 27,700 BBY,<ref name="JvS" /> the Rakata attempted an [[invasion of Korriban]] after their concerted attempts to seduce Adas failed.<ref name="END" /> Though repulsed by the dark side-fueled fury of Adas and his Sith,<ref name="BoS">''[[Book of Sith: Secrets from the Dark Side]]''</ref> the Rakata successfully killed the Sith King during the conflict's final days, sending the Sith into disarray as they made [[Korriban civil war|war]] upon each other in their attempts to capitalize upon the power vacuum left in Adas's absence.<ref name="END" /><ref name="GH05">{{TORcite|type=codex|Galactic History 05: Rise of the Infinite Empire}}</ref> During this period of strife and turmoil, a [[Kissai heretics|group of Sith]] of the [[Kissai]] [[Priest/Legends|priest]] caste<ref name="BoS" /> began to publicly interpret the dark side's failure to save Adas from death as a sign from [[The Force/Legends|the Force]] to renounce the dark side and reject the teachings of the Rakata.<ref name="KOTORCGWE5" /> Branded heretics and banished from Korriban,<ref name="TJP">[[The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force (real-life book)|''The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force'']]</ref> these exiles repurposed a captured [[Rakatan ship]] equipped with a [[Force-drive|Force-powered hyperdrive]] and set out from their homeworld into the unknown, trusting in the Force to guide them to a suitable refuge.<ref name="TEA" /> They also carried their [[Writing/Legends|writing scripts]], known as [[High Sith]] and [[Common Sith]], with them.<ref name="TWW">{{Hyperspace|url=hyperspace/source/writtenword/index.html?page=1|text=The Written Word|int=The Written Word}}</ref>

Their protracted perambulations eventually brought them to Tund, a verdant Force nexus lost upon the north-east borders of the [[Open Sea/Legends|Open Sea]] in the Centrality sector.<ref name="TEA" /> These Kissai and their descendants remained in isolation on the remote world for millennia thereafter, establishing a unique pureblooded Sith society and identity distinct from those of the mainline Sith. Convinced by their interactions with the Forceful Rakata that all sentients were Force-sensitive, the Tundan Sith espoused a monist [[Unifying Force/Legends|Unifying Force]] philosophy that rejected the traditional light side/dark side dualism of conventional philosophy and instead declared the Force to be a single, indivisible cosmic entity without sides or aspects, a conception they called "the Unity."<ref name="KOTORCGWE5" />

===Manderon Period===
{{Quote|The Sith reached other worlds, including those outside the Stygian Caldera. Tund became a prison for heretics...|An extract from the [[Sorzus Syn's chronicle|Chronicle]] of [[Sorzus Syn]], [[6900 BBY]]|<ref name="BoS" />}}
In 6900 BBY, a group of mostly [[Human/Legends|Human-blooded]] [[Dark Jedi/Legends|Dark Jedi]] known as the [[Exiles]] [[Discovery of Korriban|arrived]] on Korriban, having fled from their defeat in the [[Battle of Corbos]] at the end of the [[Hundred-Year Darkness/Legends|Hundred-Year Darkness]].<ref name="JvS" /> In the remote backwater of the Outer Rim, they discovered the Sith species, who in the intervening millennia since their legendary Sith King Adas's death had [[Sith Empire expansion|expanded]] the borders of their [[Sith Empire (Pre-Republic)|ancient Sith Empire]] outward from their homeworld to the surrounding [[Sith Worlds/Legends|Sith Worlds]] of the [[Stygian Caldera]].<ref name="TEA" /> The Exiles ascended to the rulership of the primitive Sith, employing [[Sith alchemy/Legends|Sith alchemy]] to merge their blood with that of their subjects.<ref name="BoS" /> The resultant [[Hybrid/Legends|hybrid]] race of Sith-Humans subsequently came to constitute the majority of the [[Sith Empire/Legends|reorganized Sith Empire's]] population in the centuries that followed.

Though most of the Sith Empire's holdings were concentrated in the Stygian Caldera, the Sith species had previously colonized a handful of outlying worlds prior to the Exiles' arrival, and had at some point rediscovered the pureblooded Sith enclave on Tund.<ref name="TEA" /> In her 6900 BBY chronicle, the ''[[Jen'jidai]]'' Sorzus Syn noted that the Sith employed Tund as a penal colony and ''de facto'' prison to which outcasts, exiles, and heretics were banished.<ref name="BoS" /> The Exiles' reorganized incarnation of the Sith Empire continued this practice in the years that followed, and Tund's population of pureblooded Tundan Sith was eventually joined on-world by disparate groups of half-breed Sith-Human outcasts banished from the Sith Worlds.<ref name="TEA" />

The Sith Empire met its end during the [[Great Hyperspace War/Legends|Great Hyperspace War]] of [[5000 BBY/Legends|5000 BBY]], a failed invasion of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] by the [[Sith military|forces]] of the ''[[Jen'ari]]'' [[Naga Sadow/Legends|Naga Sadow]]. A joint Republic-[[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi]] [[Post–Great Hyperspace War counterinvasion|counterinvasion]] of the Sith Empire followed,<ref name="SWTORE">''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic Encyclopedia]]''</ref> ultimately leading to the near-eradication of the Sith species as civil conflict, famine, and disease wracked the Stygian Caldera. Though some Sith continued to oppose the Republic occupation in the Sith Worlds on the battlefield,<ref name="GH30">{{TORcite|type=codex|Galactic History 30: Rise of the Sith Emperor}}</ref> many Sith-blooded refugees fled to outlying worlds as diverse as [[Dromund Kaas/Legends|Dromund Kaas]],<ref name="SWTORE" /> [[Thule/Legends|Thule]],<ref name="GatORW">''[[Geonosis and the Outer Rim Worlds]]''</ref> [[Ambria/Legends|Ambria]], [[Vjun/Legends|Vjun]], and Tund,<ref name="TEA" /> persisting in isolation in remote corners far from the Republic.

===Post-Manderon period===
{{Quote|The Sorcerers saw their abilities as a kind of magic, and presented themselves to the galaxy at large as powerful wizards...The Jedi Order...recognized their field of study as training in the Force...|An extract from Tionne Solusar's 40 BBY compendium, ''Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force''|<ref name="JvS" />}}
During the [[post-Manderon period]], the disparate groups of Sith present on Tund coalesced into a single cultural entity, eventually giving birth to a unique sect of Force users known as the [[Sorcerers of Tund/Legends|Sorcerers of Tund]] around the time of the [[Third Great Schism]].<ref name="founding">''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' maintains the Sorcerers arose after [[5000 BBY/Legends|5000 BBY]], with ''[[The New Essential Guide to Characters]]'' additionally clarifying that the group's inception occurred around the time of one of the [[Great Schism/Legends|Great Schisms]]. The only Great Schism that occurred between 5000 BBY and the rise of [[Karnak Tetsu]], the earliest Sorcerer of Tund named in [[Star Wars Legends|Legends]] canon who lived around the time of the [[Dark Wars]] of [[3955 BBY]], was the [[Third Great Schism]] of [[4250 BBY]].</ref> In keeping with the traditional kratocracy that characterized the prevailing cultural mores of the Sith species,<ref name="END" /><ref name="BoS" /> this order of Force-sensitives eventually came to rule Tund as a magocratic cabal in the centuries that followed its founding.<ref name="TEA" />

[[File:Sorcerer_of_Tund_JATM.jpg|thumb|left|250px|The Sorcerers of Tund practiced magic in isolated monastic enclaves on Tund.]]

The unique society of the Sorcerers of Tund combined the disciplines of science, ontology, and magic,<ref name="KOTORCGWE5" /> leading both outsiders and the Sorcerers themselves to view their refined power in the Force as something akin to arcane wizardry.<ref name="JvS" /><ref name="JATM" /><ref name="TDSS">''[[The Dark Side Sourcebook]]''</ref> Like their pureblooded progenitors of old, the Sorcerers of Tund likewise rejected the light side/dark side duality of the Force and proclaimed that the omnipresence of "the Unity" as evidenced in all sentient lifeforms illuminated the deceptions of duality and multiplicity as espoused by more conventional Forceful schools of thought. The Sorcerers' cosmology portrayed life&mdash;and by extension, the Force&mdash;as perfectly balanced and harmonious and considered the existence of true opposites as little more than an illusion.<ref name="KOTORCGWE5" />

Though Tund's population of Sith had managed to avoid detection by the Jedi during post–Great Hyperspace War counterinvasion,<ref name="TEA" /> the Order eventually took note of the Sorcerers of Tund during the post-Manderon period, recognizing their refined magical powers as a form of Force-sensitivity.<ref name="JvS" /> The Jedi occasionally sent emissaries and [[Jedi recruiter]]s to Tund in the hopes of persuading the Sorcerers to eschew their trappings of magic and mysticism, embrace a more conventional understanding of the Force, and join the Jedi Order.<ref name="TDSS" /> Such conversion attempts were repeatedly rebuffed by the Sorcerers,<ref name="JvS" /><ref name="TJP" /> who believed that only those of Sith blood could grasp the Force's true nature.<ref name="KOTORCGWE5" />

===Inter-Sith Wars period===
{{Quote|Deep in the Outer Rim's Centrality, [the Sorcerers] practice a secretive and malevolent style of Force manipulation, which they characterize as spellcasting. The Council has tried to recruit them, but without success.|An extract from Chief Librarian Restelly Quist's "The History of the Sith" as published in ''The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force''|<ref name="TJP" />}}
Unable to successfully convert the Sorcerers,<ref name="TJP" /> the [[Jedi High Council/Legends|Jedi High Council]] eventually opted to simply leave the Tundan Sith in peace to continue studying the Force in their own fashion.<ref name="JvS" /> The Order as a whole subsequently came to view the Sorcerers of Tund as just another Force sect akin to the [[Jal Shey]] and [[Zeison Sha]],<ref name="KOTORCGWE5" /> and were content to send occasional observers to Tund to ensure that the Sorcerers did not delve too deeply into the concerted study of the dark side.<ref name="JvS" /><ref name="JATM" /><ref name="TDSS" /> Despite their differences of belief, the Jedi Order and the Sorcerers of Tund managed to peacefully coexist without tension for some time.<ref name="JvS" />

Around the time of the [[Great Sith War/Legends|Great Sith War]], a Sith Offshoot named [[Karnak Tetsu]], to whom was applied the [[Wikipedia:Epithet|epithet]] "[[Maleficent|the Maleficent]]" in subsequent years,<ref name="TIW">{{SW|url=news/the-imperial-warlords-despoilers-of-an-empire-part-3|series=The Imperial Warlords: Despoilers of an Empire|text=Part 3|nolive=1}}</ref> ascended to the rulership of the Sorcerers of Tund. An enigmatic figure possessed of great power in the Force, Tetsu's tenure as leader of the Sorcerers was a reign of terror characterized by the study and practice of a malevolent style of Force manipulation.<ref name="TJP" /> The Force sect as a whole gradually shifted towards the dark side under Tetsu's rule.<ref name="JATM" /> In response, the restored Jedi Order, having rebounded from near-extinction in the aftermath of the [[First Jedi Purge]] and [[Dark Wars]], condemned the Sorcerers and recategorized the group's hermetica and associated doctrine as unqualified heresy.<ref name="KOTORCGWE5" />

===Great Peace of the Republic===
{{Quote|We are not some cult like Tetsu's Sorcerers of Tund.|[[Darth Plagueis/Legends|Darth Plagueis]], to his apprentice, [[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious]]|<ref name="DP" />}}
Over time, as wars with the mainline Sith factions continued to dominate the Jedi Order's attentions, fewer and fewer Jedi observers were sent to Tund to monitor the Sorcerers.<ref name="JATM" /> The last recorded visit to Tund by emissaries of the Order occurred more than a thousand years before the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]], sometime prior to the defeat of [[Skere Kaan]] and the end of the [[Ruusan campaign]].<ref name="JvS" /><ref name="TDSS" /> Tionne Solusar, in her 40 ABY compendium titled ''Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force'', posited that the Jedi may have sought to enlist the Sorcerers in their fight against the Sith, though the nature of their final visit to Tund remained a subject of speculation alone.<ref name="JvS" />

The Jedi Order eventually forgot about the existence of the Sorcerers altogether by the time of the [[Great Peace of the Republic]],<ref name="JvS" /><ref name="TDSS" /> leaving the Sith-blooded Force users in isolation on their backwater world.<ref name="JATM" /> However, the [[Order of the Sith Lords]], a vestigial remnant of the mainline Sith that persisted in secret through the [[Golden Age of the Old Republic]], were aware of the existence of the Sorcerers and familiar with the history of prominent members like Tetsu. Though Darth Plagueis, the presiding [[Dark Lord of the Sith|Dark Lord]] of the Banite Sith, dismissed the Sorcerers as a "cult,"<ref name="DP">[[Darth Plagueis (novel)|''Darth Plagueis'']]</ref> his [[Sith apprentice/Legends|apprentice]], Darth Sidious, recognized the Sorcerers' religious teachings as archaic interpretations of ancient Sith doctrine<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> and harbored a desire to possess the Sorcerers' secrets for himself.<ref name="TEA" /><ref name="JvS" /><ref name="NEGtC" />

In [[45 BBY/Legends|45 BBY]], a pair of [[Comet/Legends|comets]] struck the planet [[Toong'l/Legends|Toong'l]], poisoning the world and forcing its native population of [[Toong/Legends|Toongs]] to relocate offworld. Many refugees of this species ended up colonizing nearby Tund, grateful for its small population and jungle biomes.<ref name="TEA" /><ref name="TCSWEIII267" /> Culturally reticent towards outsiders by nature,<ref name="KOTORCGWE5" /> the Sorcerers of Tund did not take kindly to the presence of non-Sith on their ancestral homeworld, and spent the next several decades persecuting the Toongs. The [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]], secretly Darth Sidious, readily capitalized upon the outrage their actions generated in the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]]. Encouraging the public perception of the Sorcerers as self-important charlatans, Palpatine used the persecution of the Toongs as a pretext to intervene on Tund, though the agents he sent to the planet instead secretly scoured the world for hidden Sith knowledge.<ref name="TEA" />

===Imperial Period===
{{Quote|I don't see potential for recruitment here. The Navy can contain Tund.|Handwritten notes by Emperor Palpatine dismissing the possibility of enlisting the Sorcerers of Tund as [[Dark side adept/Legends|Dark Side Adepts]]|<ref name="TJP" />}}
Despite his awareness of the fact that the doctrine of the Sorcerers of Tund was based on ancient Sith teachings,<ref name="JvS" /><ref name="NEC" /> the newly crowned Emperor Palpatine dismissed the possibility of recruiting the Sorcerers to serve as [[Dark side adept/Legends|Dark Side Adepts]] of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], considering instead deploying the [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Imperial Navy]] to blockade Tund and confine the Sorcerers to their homeworld.<ref name="TJP" /> Nonetheless, the Emperor retained a strong interest the Sorcerers and the acquisition of their hoarded dark-sided lore during the [[Imperial Era/Legends|Imperial Period]].<ref name="JvS" /><ref name="NEC" />

Sometime prior to 5 BBY,<ref name="TEA" /><ref name="TDSS" /> Rokur Gepta, a snail-like [[Croke]] hailing from the [[Unknown Regions/Legends|Unknown Regions]],<ref name="NEGtC" /> managed to apply his species's natural powers of illusion and shapeshifting<ref name="TDSS" /> to a successful infiltration of the Sorcerers. The Croke studied the group's Sith teachings and co-opted its secrets for his own purposes during his tenure on Tund.<ref name="NEGtC" /> Once he had learned all he could from his teachers,<ref name="TDSS" /> Gepta unleashed a biological weapon and an electromagnetic torpedo upon Tund. The resultant green fire generated by the weapons eradicated all life on the planet and poisoned its atmosphere, rendering the irradiated husk of Tund uninhabitable.<ref name="TEA" /><ref name="TCSWEIII267" /><ref name="JvS" /><ref name="NEGtC" />

Either in exchange for Tundan secrets or out of respect for the Croke's abilities, Emperor Palpatine eventually named Gepta the presiding [[Scrivinir]] of the Centrality and provided him a decommissioned Imperial cruiser named the ''[[Wennis]]'' with which to consolidate his control over the remote region of space.<ref name="NEGtC" /><ref name="TDSS" /> The Croke often returned Tund in the days that followed, meditating in a small enclave protected from the radioactive atmosphere by a system of force fields.<ref name="TCSWEIII267" /><ref name="NEGtC" /> Though the Croke harbored ambitions of overthrowing Palpatine and ruling [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] in his stead,<ref name="TDSS" /> Gepta was eventually [[Death/Legends|killed]] in single combat with [[Lando Calrissian/Legends|Lando Calrissian]] less than a year after Tund's destruction,<ref name="NEGtC" /> bringing an end to the ancient order of Force users to which he had belonged.<ref name="JvS" /><ref name="TDSS" /><ref name="NEC" />

===Post-Imperial era===
{{Quote|Following the invasion of Korriban by the Rakata, the Sith gained access to their rudimentary hyperspace technology, and carried these scripts to worlds such as Ziost, Jaguada, and Tund.|A mention of Tund extracted from an article "The Written Word" by Dr. Milanda Vorgan, 38 ABY|<ref name="TWW" />}}
In [[38 ABY]], the world was mentioned in the [[Xenolinguist/Legends|xenolinguist]] Doctor [[Milanda Vorgan]]'s article "[[The Written Word: A Brief Introduction to the Writing Systems of Galactic Basic]]."<ref name="TWW" />

==Inhabitants==
{{Main|Sorcerers of Tund/Legends|Toong/Legends}}
{{Quote|To the best of my knowledge, nobody was ever sure what species the Tund wizards were, or even if they were all members of the same species. But I knew a thing or two about the sorcerers, like that they're boringly mysterious and given to flashy entrances...|Extract from Lando Calrissian's [[22 ABY/Legends|22 ABY]] memoir, ''[[How to Succeed in Everything]]''|<ref name="JvS" />}}
Immediately prior to its destruction at the hands of Rokur Gepta in 5 BBY,<ref name="TDSS" /> the planet Tund boasted a total population of eighteen million sentients. The species mix primarily consisted of approximately thirteen million, one hundred and forty thousand Toong (seventy-three percent of the population); one million, two hundred and sixty thousand pureblooded Sith (seven percent); and a diverse assortment of other species numbering approximately three million, six hundred thousand beings (twenty percent).<ref name="TEA" />

[[File:Tund.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Tund came to host a Toong diaspora in the years following 45 BBY.]]

The pureblooded Sith residents of Tund were the descendants of several disparate groups; namely, the original Kissai heretics banished from Korriban after the death of Sith King Adas,<ref name="KOTORCGWE5" /> the outcasts exiled from the ancient Sith Empire prior to the arrival of the Dark Jedi Exiles,<ref name="BoS" /> the half-breed Sith-Human exiles who settled Tund during the era of the old Sith Empire,<ref name="TEA" /> and the various Sith-blooded refugees who flocked to the planet in the years following the Great Hyperspace War.<ref name="KOTORCGWE5" /> Of these Sith, the Force-using Sorcerers of Tund constituted the magocratic cabal that ruled the planet for much of its modern history.<ref name="TEA" /> The Sorcerers presented themselves as magic-wielding wizards to the outside galaxy,<ref name="JvS" /> and spent much of their time at their monastic enclaves in concerted study of the Force and in the perfecting of dark-sided rituals.<ref name="JATM" /><ref name="TDSS" />

Towards the end of its recorded history, the planet hosted a sizable population of Toong who settled Tund in the aftermath of their homeworld's destruction. Drawn to the planet for its small population and jungle environment, the Toong found themselves in conflict with the native Sith-blooded Tundan natives, but persisted on the planet despite their persecution at the hands of the Sorcerers of Tund.<ref name="TEA" /> Among the more notable members of this Toong diaspora was [[Ben Quadinaros/Legends|Ben Quadinaros]], a male Toong who participated in the [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]] [[Boonta Eve Classic/Legends#The race of 32 BBY|Boonta Eve Classic]] [[Podracing/Legends|podracing]] championship on [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]].<ref name="TPM">{{Film|I}}</ref>

Though [[Old High Trammic/Legends|Old High Trammic]]&mdash;a language derived from the ancient tongue of the Sharu&mdash;saw regular use as the common trade language of the Centrality sector,<ref name="ACGttC" /> a number of other diverse languages were likewise spoken with some degree of regularity on Tund prior to its destruction. While the Sith-blooded population of Tund primarily spoke the ancient [[Sith (language)|Sith language]],<ref name="TEA" /> the Sorcerers of Tund likewise employed [[Tundan]],<ref name="KOTORCGWE5" /><ref name="TDSS" /> a language that also saw usage by certain offworld Force users<ref name="KOTORCG">''[[Knights of the Old Republic Campaign Guide]]''</ref> and poets.<ref name="SWEGTWAC">{{SW|url=news/the-essential-guide-to-warfare-authors-cut-part-3-xim-the-despot|series=Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare Author's Cut|text=Part 3 - "Xim the Despot"}}</ref> The Toong population primarily spoke their native language [[Toongese]].<ref name="UAA" />

==Locations==
{{Quote|Tund is now an uninhabited, irradiated wasteland, and the death of Gepta marked an end to the Sorcerers of Tund.|An extract from [[Voren Na'al/Legends|Voren Na'al's]] [[The New Essential Chronology (in-universe)|''The New Essential Chronology'']]|<ref name="NEC" />}}
An isolated planet far from the major population centers of the Centrality,<ref name="TEA" /> Tund was a shadowy world largely unprobed by the greater [[galactic community]].<ref name="ACGttC" /> During its protracted tenure as the headquarters and homeworld of the Sorcerers of Tund,<ref name="TEA" /><ref name="JvS" /><ref name="NEC" /> the planet's surface played host to a number of isolated monastic enclaves<ref name="JATM" /><ref name="TDSS" /> in which the Sith-blooded Sorcerers studied the mystical arts and searched for a better understanding of the galaxy and the powers that held it together. These structures, similar in purpose to the ancient Sith [[library-temple]]s that once dotted the Sith Worlds,<ref name="TotJC">''[[Tales of the Jedi Companion]]''</ref> often took the form of inverted conical towers overlooking the planet's varied forests and escarpments.<ref name="JATM" />

With the planet's subsequent colonization by Toong refugees fleeing the destruction of their homeworld Toong'l in 45 BBY, the planet likewise came to a host a number of Toong settlements scattered throughout the planet's jungle biospheres.<ref name="TEA" /> Toong structures on Tund generally took the form of multi-level circular buildings crowned with green domes, adorned with copious arches and a multiplicity of windows, and surrounded by decorative fences and gates.<ref name="TCSWEIII267" />

==Behind the scenes==
The PC game [[Star Wars: Rebellion (video game)|''Star Wars: Rebellion'']] mistakenly places Tund in the [[Xappyh sector/Legends|Xappyh sector]]. In early scripts of [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']], the podracer [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]] [[Slide Paramita]] was said to have originated from Tund. However, Paramita was ultimately cut from the script and Tund was repurposed to serve as the homeworld of the Toong podracer pilot Ben Quadinaros.

The question of Tund's status as a formal member world of the Sith Empire has never been directly addressed by any [[Star Wars Legends|Legends]] source, despite a multiplicity of reference materials both confirming some degree of affiliation between the two groups and corroborating the Empire's usage of the world as a penal colony for Sith-blooded outcasts and heretics. However, [[Daniel Wallace]], co-author of ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'', indicated in private correspondence that though he was unsure whether he personally drafted the lore behind the ''Atlas''{{'s}} entry on Tund, it is his unofficial opinion that Tund was likely a formal member world of the Sith Empire. His personal take on the subject of Tund's status seems to be tacitly corroborated by the various other references to Tund and the Sith Empire scattered throughout the ''Atlas''{{'s}} contents.
